subject: biology
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE Biology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.blurb: Cells, photosynthesis, nutrition, respiration, coordination and ecology

units.name: Unit 2 — Body Systems, Genetics, Microorganisms & Health
units.blurb: Transport, circulation, genetics, reproduction, variation and health

units.name: Unit 3 — Practical Skills
units.blurb: Prescribed practicals, experimental method, data handling and analysis

topics.name: Cells
topics.blurb: Animal, plant and bacterial cell structure and microscopy

topics.name: Food & Energy

topics.name: Enzymes & Digestion
topics.blurb: Enzyme action and the human digestive system

topics.name: Respiratory System & Cell Respiration
topics.blurb: Breathing, gas exchange and aerobic/anaerobic respiration

topics.name: Coordination & Control

topics.name: Ecological Relationships & Energy Flow
topics.blurb: Food chains, energy flow, cycles and measuring biodiversity

topics.name: Osmosis & Plant Transport
topics.blurb: Osmosis, water relations, transpiration and translocation

topics.name: The Circulatory System
topics.blurb: Heart, blood vessels, blood and the kidneys

connections.why: Cell-membrane structure controls osmosis and the movement of water in and out of cells
DNA in the nucleus is copied when cells divide and is passed on through inheritance
Glucose made in photosynthesis is the fuel released by respiration
Plant transport tissues carry the water and sugars photosynthesis needs and produces
Digestive enzymes break down the food groups into absorbable nutrients
Enzymes catalyse digestion and the controlled reactions of respiration
Energy in food is released for the body through respiration
The circulatory system delivers oxygen and glucose to respiring cells and removes CO2
Hormones coordinate the menstrual cycle, fertility and contraception
Inherited genetic variation is what natural selection acts upon
Meiosis in reproduction halves chromosome number and mixes alleles
Sexual reproduction generates the variation selection can act on
Competition within ecosystems drives natural selection
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that then flows through every food chain
Kidney function and tissue fluid both depend on osmosis and water balance
Pathogens and white blood cells are carried around the body in the blood
Microorganisms and their enzymes are used in food production and biotechnology
Bacterial and viral structure explains how microorganisms cause disease
Investigating the effect of temperature on enzymes is a prescribed practical
Testing a leaf for starch to show photosynthesis is a prescribed practical
Investigating osmosis in plant tissue is a prescribed practical
Using quadrats to sample abundance in a habitat is a prescribed practical
Carrying out food tests for sugars, starch, protein and fat is a prescribed practical
